topic.title: Exploration with Sparse Rewards and Changing Environments
topic.overview: An agent must discover useful behavior even when external rewards are rare or delayed. These papers develop intrinsic rewards, reward-free exploration, optimism, and information-seeking policies. Some methods use both past and possible future transitions to recognize bottlenecks, while others exploit structure in the reward function itself.
topic.whyItMatters: Visiting many states is not necessarily informative exploration. Effective strategies should reveal controllable routes, resolve uncertainty relevant to future tasks, and avoid confusing randomness or repeated failure with useful novelty.
topic.evolution: The collection spans active exploration from the early 1990s to optimistic model selection and modern reward-agnostic navigation. Recent work incorporates retrospective transition structure and constraint-aware intrinsic rewards. Newer examples address environmental drift and combine low-rank reward completion with uncertainty-based fallback to exploration when structural assumptions are unreliable.
openQuestions: Which intrinsic objectives discover reusable knowledge rather than task-irrelevant novelty?
How can an agent recognize when a structural reward model should be abandoned?
